correctness.rationale: Navarro Aznar's Chern-class formula gives the displayed surface Euler formula. For a balancing move \((x,y)\mapsto(x+1,y-1)\), the exact change is \(P\delta(C-B-\delta)\). In codimension two the sign factor is \((x-1)^2+(y-2)^2-2\), negative only for \((x,y)=(1,3)\), yielding the 64-to-63 reversal. With at least one remaining shifted degree, the extra term \((x+y-2)R+H\ge3\) makes every genuine balancing move strictly positive. Iterating balancing and reverse-balancing gives the unique extrema. The actual artifact verifier was inspected and independently checks the formula and predicted extrema over a broad finite range; the theorem itself is symbolic.

final_claim: For smooth complex complete-intersection surfaces of fixed codimension \(c\ge2\) and fixed sum \(S\) of defining degrees, the Euler characteristic (and hence \(b_2\)) is uniquely maximized by the balanced multidegree and minimized by the one-heavy multidegree, except for the unique codimension-two reversal at \(S=6\), where \((2,4)\) has \(\chi=64\) and \((3,3)\) has \(\chi=63\).
limitations: All defining degrees are at least two and the ground field is \(\mathbb C\).
Codimension is fixed; singular, weighted-projective, or varying-codimension comparisons are not covered.
